featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Malvan Tadka in Mulund offers a fairly comfortable introduction to coastal cuisine, though the overall experience leans more toward a North Indian palate than an authentically bold Malvani one. The food is decent and satisfying in parts, but if you’re expecting deeply robust, coconut-forward, fiery coastal gravies, you may find the flavours slightly toned down and more mainstream.

Over multiple visits, we’ve tried a wide range of their menu. The Surmai Fry remains one of the better choices — fresh, nicely marinated, and well cooked. The Pomfret Fry, Bangda Fry, and Bombil Fry are competently done, while the Stuffed Bombil Fry stands out as one of the more memorable dishes — flavourful and prepared with care. Seafood combinations featuring Kolambi Masala, prawn preparations, and even seasonal Crab Masala offer variety, though the gravies sometimes feel milder than traditional Malvani spice profiles.

Among the non-seafood options, the Chicken (Malvani style), Mutton preparations, Chicken Masala, Chicken Sukka, and Mutton Sukka are decent, but again lean toward a safer, more North Indian-style gravy base rather than a distinctly coastal punch. However, the Chicken Gharguti Handi was exceptionally good — homely, balanced, and far more flavourful than expected. It’s easily one of the highlights of the meal.

Accompaniments like Neer Dosa, Bhakri, and Kombdi Vade (when available) pair well with the curries, and the Solkadhi offers a refreshing coastal touch to round off the meal.

Overall, Malvan Tadka delivers average, serviceable food with a few standout dishes like the Chicken Gharguti Handi and Stuffed Bombil Fry elevating the experience. It may not fully satisfy purists seeking strong Malvani authenticity, but for those looking for a milder, more accessible version of coastal cuisine in Mulund, it does an okay job. A balanced three-star experience — pleasant, but not particularly distinctive.

Another issue was with the order-taking experience. The staff member assisting us (Priya) seemed unsure about certain dishes, their preparation, and recommendations. On one occasion, our requirements were not fully understood, and it felt like the focus was more on pushing the “highlight of the day” rather than explaining the dish properly and understanding what we were actually looking for.

Additionally, there appeared to be some visible internal disagreement among the staff, which unfortunately became noticeable at our table. As guests, we were not particularly comfortable being exposed to internal banter or tension during the dining experience.

Overall, the food may have been decent, but the customer service felt overwhelming rather than welcoming. I hope this feedback is taken constructively, because the experience could be improved significantly.

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Sindhudurg Family Dining to celebrate a birthday, and overall it was a mixed experience.

The restaurant is very conveniently located, especially for people coming from Mulund East railway station. The management is also supportive for small celebrations like birthdays, so that’s a plus.

However, the space is quite compact with tight seating. It can feel a bit congested, and there’s definitely room for improvement in terms of space management and comfort.

Service is another area that needs attention. There was noticeable delay in serving orders, and it seemed to be a common issue across tables, not just ours.

Coming to food:

Starters like Bombil Fry, Crab Lollipop, and Chicken Tikka Kebab were good in taste. The Crab Lollipop was the highlight.

We tried Rawas and Surmai Thalis. Surmai was fresh and tasty, while Rawas was just average. The fish curry in the thali was quite bland.

Prawns Malvani Masala and Pomfret Tawa Fry were disappointing. The prawns dish had an overpowering coconut taste, and the pomfret didn’t feel very fresh.

Chicken Sukha was flavorful and well-prepared, but Kombdi Vade didn’t feel authentic—it was more like a puri.

Surmai Tawa Fry (ordered later) was again very good.

Solkadhi was impressive and better than many nearby seafood places.

One more thing to note is the portion size—it felt a bit less for the price, so overall it came across as slightly expensive for the quantity served.

Overall, it’s a decent place for seafood with some really good dishes, but consistency, authenticity, service speed, and portion sizing need improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Sony service
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Sea Salt Fire, Thane recently and had a truly satisfying Maharashtrian dining experience. The place beautifully blends authentic flavours with a modern presentation.

We started with Paneer Kasturi Malai Tikka, which was super soft, creamy and perfectly marinated. The Shevga Fry was a pleasant surprise – nicely spiced and cooked just right.

For drinks, the Strawberry Mint Sparkle and Thai Mango Twist were refreshing, while the Solkadhi gave that perfect traditional touch to the meal.

In mains, the Pahadi Saag Paneer was rich and flavourful. Paired it with Tandlachi Bhakari and Tandoori Butter Roti, both fresh and well made. The highlight was the Hirvya Vatnichi Veg Biryani – aromatic, masaledar and full of authentic Maharashtrian taste.

Desserts were the real showstoppers!
The Benami Kheer had a unique and unexpected twist which made it stand out, and the Chocolate Strawberry Mousse was rich, smooth and a perfect way to end the meal.

Overall, great food, good portion sizes, and a satisfying experience for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian cuisine in Thane. Definitely worth visiting with family.

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re anywhere near Paanch Rasta in Mulund West and looking for a place that delivers both exceptional food and genuinely warm hospitality, Sandeep Restaurant & Bar is a spot you should not miss.

In a city like Mumbai, where dining options are endless, what truly sets a restaurant apart is consistency and the way they treat their guests. Sandeep Restaurant excels at both.

Let’s start with the food. Their Prawns Koliwada is an absolute must try. Perfectly marinated, crisp on the outside, juicy inside, and seasoned just right. It carries that authentic coastal flavour without being overly greasy or heavy. The Butter Chicken is rich, balanced and comforting, with a smooth gravy that pairs beautifully with naan or jeera rice. And the Fish Curry deserves a special mention. Fresh, flavourful and well spiced, it feels homely yet restaurant refined at the same time. You can tell that quality ingredients and experience go into every dish.

However, what truly elevates the experience is the hospitality. The entire staff operates with professionalism, attentiveness and warmth that feels rare today. They are quick without being intrusive, polite without being mechanical, and genuinely attentive to every table. There is a sense of discipline and care in the way they coordinate service, which makes dining here smooth and enjoyable.

A special appreciation for the lead staff member, Satish Anna. His presence on the floor reflects leadership and experience. He ensures everything runs seamlessly and makes guests feel personally welcomed. That kind of involvement from senior staff creates a big difference in overall experience.
Sandeep Restaurant is not just about good food. It is about feeling valued as a guest. Whether you are coming with family, friends or colleagues, you can expect consistent quality, generous portions and a team that truly understands hospitality.

Highly recommended for anyone in and around Mulund West looking for a reliable, satisfying and welcoming dining experience

The manager is extremely rude and doesn’t even bother to answer calls. When I tried calling to complain about an incorrect order, he hung up on me mid-conversation — very unprofessional.

The food quality has also gone down noticeably. The ingredients don’t taste as fresh as they once did, and the overall flavor has become quite average.

But the biggest disappointment is the attitude of the staff and management. They clearly don’t care about regular or family customers anymore — it feels like they only want to cater to drunkards.

It’s sad to see such a reputed restaurant lose its charm because of poor management and arrogance. I genuinely hope they improve, but for now, I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Tushar Sinagare
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this well-known restaurant Nisarga Restuarant, Mulund, reputed for its lip-smacking fish and chicken dishes, for a family dinner. Unfortunately, our experience did not fully meet expectations.

Ambience & Seating

The initial seating arrangement was inconvenient, as the restaurant couldn't immediately provide adjacent tables for our group of eight. We were seated at two opposite-facing tables. However, after some time, the manager arranged an adjacent setup once another family left, which was appreciated.

Service

The service left room for improvement. Our starter was served later than expected, and one of the signature dishes, fish ghassi, was unavailable. Instead, we opted for fish Malvani, which took 15-20 minutes to arrive.

Food Quality

Vegetarian Dishes: Surprisingly, the vegetarian options stole the show. The Manchow soup, spring rolls, and hara bhara kabab were flavorful and arrived promptly. The mix veg gravy and paneer 65 in the main course were well-cooked and delicious.

Non-Vegetarian Dishes: The fish Malvani was decent but lacked the wow factor expected from a restaurant known for its non-veg specialties.

Overall Experience

While the vegetarian dishes impressed, the delays, unavailability of popular items, and initial seating issues took away from the overall experience.

Rating: 3.5/5

Would recommend this place for vegetarian options but with tempered expectations for service and availability of non-veg dishes.

featured_reviews.review_text:
As a kid, I’ve been to Sindhudurg countless times, from spontaneous Sunday lunches with my family to special celebrations like birthdays and anniversaries. No matter how many years have passed, one thing that has remained beautifully consistent is their authentic Malvani flavour and unmatched freshness of seafood. It’s rare to find a place that maintains such high standards for decades and Sindhudurg has managed to do just that.
Recently, I hosted my mom’s retirement dinner here for her and her colleagues and we had the pleasure of dining in their “baithak” which is a cozy, exclusive space that offers a sense of privacy and warmth. The staff made sure everything ran smoothly, from the service to the presentation. It truly felt personal and thoughtfully managed, just like a home-style feast with restaurant level perfection.
Coming to the food, we ordered a spread that showcased the best of what Sindhudurg has to offer: Prawns Thali, Pomfret Thali, Surmai Thali, Chicken Sukkha Thali, Mutton Sukkha Thali and even one Veg Thali for variety. Alongside, we couldn’t resist their legendary Prawns Tawa Fry, Bheja Fry, and Bombil Fry, each dish bursting with coastal spice, balanced heat and that signature freshness only Sindhudurg delivers.
Every bite took me back to my childhood memories, reminding me why this place is more than just a restaurant, it’s an emotion for anyone who grew up around Thane. Highly recommend it to anyone craving authentic Malvani comfort food served with consistency, warmth and heart.
A timeless coastal gem that never disappoints!

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Godase
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hotel Sindhudurg in Thane is a well-known and much-loved restaurant, especially famous for its authentic Malvani and Maharashtrian non-vegetarian cuisine. For food lovers in Thane who enjoy spicy flavors, traditional recipes, and fresh seafood, Hotel Sindhudurg has become a trusted and popular dining destination. The restaurant truly represents the rich coastal food culture of Maharashtra right in the heart of Thane.
The biggest attraction of Hotel Sindhudurg, Thane, is its excellent seafood selection. Dishes prepared using fresh fish, prawns, crabs, and other seafood items are the highlights of the menu. The seafood is cooked in traditional Malvani style, using coconut-based gravies, kokum, and strong yet balanced spices. Popular seafood curries are full of flavor and have the perfect level of spiciness that Malvani cuisine is known for. Seafood lovers across Thane often visit the hotel specifically for these dishes.
Apart from seafood, Hotel Sindhudurg in Thane is also famous for its non-vegetarian Maharashtrian dishes. Items like chicken, mutton, and traditional curries are prepared with authentic masalas that give a bold and spicy taste. The food reflects true Maharashtrian spice levels, making it ideal for those who enjoy hot, flavorful meals. Bhakri, rice, and solkadhi served with the food complete the authentic Malvani dining experience.
The taste and consistency at Hotel Sindhudurg, Thane, are highly appreciated. The flavors remain the same over time, which builds trust among regular customers. The food is neither overly oily nor artificial in taste, maintaining a homely yet restaurant-style balance. This consistency makes the hotel a favorite spot for families and non-veg food lovers in Thane.
Cleanliness and hygiene are well maintained at Hotel Sindhudurg, Thane. The dining area is neat, tables are cleaned regularly, and the overall atmosphere is simple and comfortable. The service staff is polite, attentive, and experienced in handling customer requests, which adds to a pleasant dining experience.
Another positive point is the reasonable pricing. Considering the quality, quantity, and authentic taste of seafood and non-veg dishes, Hotel Sindhudurg in Thane offers good value for money. This makes it a popular choice among working professionals, families, and seafood lovers from different parts of Thane.
Though the restaurant focuses more on food quality than luxury interiors, its simple setup suits the traditional feel of Malvani cuisine. Minor improvements in décor could enhance the ambiance, but the powerful taste of the food remains the main attraction.
In conclusion, Hotel Sindhudurg, Thane, is a top choice for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Malvani seafood, spicy Maharashtrian non-veg cuisine, and traditional flavors. For seafood lovers in Thane who appreciate bold spices and coastal recipes, Hotel Sindhudurg is a must-visit restaurant and a true taste of Maharashtra.

My family and I have been regulars at The Food Studio for over 14 years, and it has never disappointed. The food is consistently top-notch, and the service is warm, attentive, and thoughtful. Their attentiveness was exceptional, they anticipated our needs even before we had to mention them. That level of care truly makes all the difference.

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
Two areas of improvement would be allowing customers to choose two different mocktails under the offer, especially since all mocktails are priced the same.

Another thing to improve is the coordination between staff members—there was a noticeable communication gap while placing our order.

Visited The Food Studio near Nahur Railway Station and had a generally pleasant experience. We were seated within 5 minutes, and the ambiance was nice with a large TV setup in the center, adding a lively vibe to the place.

We started with French fries and a few starters: Jhinga Koliwada, Makhmali Kumbh, Pomfret Tandoori, and Chicken Burnt Garlic. The Jhinga Koliwada was the highlight—crispy and flavorful. Makhmali Kumbh is a great vegetarian option, stuffed with cheese and tasted quite good. However, the Pomfret Tandoori didn’t meet expectations—the masala lacked punch.

For the main course, we ordered Sabzi Peshawari with roti. It leaned towards the sweeter side, possibly due to the mix of paneer, mushrooms, and green peas. Not bad if you enjoy mildly sweet gravies.

We also tried the mocktail Mulokai under their Buy 1 Get 1 Free offer. The taste was average.

Overall, a good experience with room for a few improvements.

I recently visited this place for the first time, attracted by Dineout's 50% off offer. Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing. The food was average, but the service was subpar.

1. The 50% discount was not applicable to all food items, which I discovered only after inquiring. Nearby tables were also arguing with staff about the same issue, as they had been given separate bills - one with the discount and another without.

We ate banana leaf chicken, gravy chicken lollipop and prawns tandoori..... Each and every dish is super delicious and yum... ❤️

Our bill was around 1400 rs.

Fri, sat and sun evenings are crowded, weekdays are fine to go.

Give it a try place. Thank me later 😅

Later, we had conversation with staff he said, from 3 years they serving food from small stall and now they turned into this big one... Mehnat ka fal ✨🙏🏻

featured_reviews.name: Alexzander Vicklif
featured_reviews.review_text: Sholka Dining Bar offers a lovely ambience that's perfect for a night out. The service is commendable, and the food is delicious, living up to expectations. However, the song playlist could use a serious upgrade. It really takes away from the otherwise pleasant vibe. Weekends tend to get very crowded, so plan accordingly. While the experience is enjoyable overall, it is on the pricier side.

featured_reviews.name: Sid
featured_reviews.review_text:
Highly recommend dining option for family. After renovation the ambience for indoor dining is welcoming. Outdoor sitting area has smoking zone.

Waiting times can be high in late evening / weekends.

Non-veg food prep is very tasty, with juicy and flavourful chicken dishes. Recommend angara kebab, anda gadbad, chicken neer dosa, triple shezwan fried rice.

Outdoor seating has projector showing matches.

Home delivery/ parcel can be ordered by calling the restaurant directly.

featured_reviews.name: Raj M
featured_reviews.review_text:
Crowded. Limited seating inside.

Welcome party at embrace is an almost solid wall of smokers who don't even look away when you're trying to enter with young children.

Food is wildly inconsistent - the paneer was good but the chicken tikka was ordinary.

Food service is pathetic with waiters forgetting orders. They also tend to go away and not return for long durations. But the door and valet staff are very helpful.

featured_reviews.name: sitikantha rath
featured_reviews.review_text:
